codespace_context.description: A modular cross-platform Flutter application for laboratory instrument control, battery cycling telemetry, iCharger serial communications, Autolab potentiostat/galvanostat impedance configurations, WebSocket client/server networking, and precision countdown timers.
codespace_context.current_status: Initial implementation complete with multi-screen UI, mock serial telemetry, and local CSV logging. Ready for hardware integration, protocol parsing, and platform-specific driver enhancements.

architecture.navigation: Drawer navigation in HomeScreen with dynamically rendered view widgets

screens_and_components.description: Main application scaffold featuring a navigation Drawer with icons for each sub-screen, switching active views via state index.
Basic serial monitor displaying device scan results, baud rate selection (9600 to 115200), port connection triggers, and real-time voltage display.
Comprehensive battery testing interface with input parameters (Battery Name, Nominal Voltage, Capacity in mAh), real-time serial listener hook, and automatic CSV logging via path_provider and IOSink.

Electrochemical impedance/potentiostat configuration form supporting Current Range (10nA to 1A), Bandwidth of EI, Setpoint DC, DSG Input switch, Wave Signal (Sine, 5/15 sines), Number of Cycles, Integration Time, and Frequency Sweep Start.
WebSocket client manager with configurable server URL (default ws://echo.websocket.events), real-time duplex log terminal, and command dispatcher (e.g. PING_TELEMETRY).
Precision countdown timer with visual circular layout, Start/Pause/Reset state controls, quick duration preset chips (5, 10, 30, 60 min), and custom minute input.
Hardware and communication link status dashboard showing diagnostics and system operational state.
Hardware abstraction layer handling USB port enumeration, connection lifecycle (DTR/RTS assertions, 8N1 framing), stream subscription, raw telemetry callback invocation, and voltage updates.
Remote network telemetry layer handling WebSocket lifecycle, incoming stream listener, error handlers, and string command sinks.

senior_flutter_architect_notes.observation: The 'usb_serial' package is primarily tailored for Android USB OTG / Host API. On desktop Windows/Linux/macOS, calling UsbSerial.listDevices() will not detect native COM ports. For native Windows support, integrate 'flutter_libserialport' or custom win32 serial FFI bindings.

In 'UsbService.connect()', 'liveVoltage = 3.250;' is currently a static mock. When parsing live iCharger responses (e.g., Junsi iCharger Modbus/binary or ASCII telemetry stream), implement a stream transformer with regex/binary frame delimiter matching.

In 'HomeScreen', views are rendered as 'body: _screens[_currentIndex]'. To preserve user input state (e.g., partially entered Autolab parameters or running timer displays) when switching drawer tabs, wrap views in an 'IndexedStack' or keep state via 'AutomaticKeepAliveClientMixin'.

When deployed in GitHub Codespaces or Flutter Web, 'dart:io' (File, IOSink) used in IChargerCyclingScreen is unsupported. Implement conditional exports with Web Blob downloads (e.g., 'dart:html' or 'universal_html' AnchorElement) for CSV exports.

README.md.content:
# Lab Control Suite & iCharger Tool

Cross-platform laboratory automation and battery cycling telemetry tool supporting Windows Desktop, GitHub Codespaces (Flutter Web), and Android/Linux/macOS.

---

## 1. Quick Verification & Diagnostics

### Run Serial Hardware & Windows COM Diagnostic:
Checks active COM ports across Registry (`SERIALCOMM`), WMI/CIM, and PnP entities, recognizing FTDI, Silicon Labs CP210x, QinHeng CH340, Prolific PL2303, and Arduino CDC devices:
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\diagnose_ports.ps1 -TestAccess
```

### Run Automated Architecture & Resilience Verification:
Tests Windows COM path normalization (`COM1-9` vs `\\.\COM10+`), exponential backoff jitter bounds, chipset recognition, and `EACCES`/`BUSY` error boundaries:
```cmd
dart run scripts\verify_serial_windows.dart
```

---

## 2. Windows Desktop Execution

### Prerequisites:
```cmd
flutter --version
flutter config --enable-windows-desktop
```

### Health check & dependency fetch:
```cmd
flutter doctor
cd lab
flutter pub get
flutter analyze
flutter test
```

### Run Windows Desktop App:
```cmd
flutter run -d windows
```

---

## 3. GitHub Codespaces / Web Execution
To run in browser from a Codespace:
```bash
cd lab
flutter run -d web-server --web-port 8080 --web-hostname 0.0.0.0
```

---

## 4. Node.js Serial-to-WebSocket Bridge (Optional Headless Daemon)

When running Flutter on Web or in remote client-server setups, use the high-performance Node.js Serial Bridge located in `serial_bridge/`:

```cmd
cd serial_bridge
npm install
npm run check-env
npm run diagnose
npm start
```
The bridge listens on `ws://127.0.0.1:8080` and streams serial telemetry directly to Flutter's `NetworkService`.

---

## 5. Configuration Files

- [`config/serial_config.json`](config/serial_config.json): Dynamic baud rates, exponential backoff timing, and known USB chipset matrix.
- [`.env.example`](.env.example): Environment variable templates for ports, bauds, and WebSocket servers.
